messages:
maia: FYI customer ACME hit a parsing failure when using response_format strict=true. They get a 200 but the body is an HTML error page (unexpected token on client). Started after a model rollout.
kyle: Can you paste the exact request + response headers and the response_format payload they used? Need to repro.
maia: Sure — redacting keys but exact shape below:
```bash
curl -X POST \"https://api.redwood.com/v1/responses\" \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -H \"Accept: application/json\" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-v2","input":"generate structured output","response_format":{"type":"json","json_schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"answer":{"type":"string"}},"required":["answer"]},"strict":true}}'
```
Response (from customer):
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8
X-Request-Id: rq_abc123

<html>\n<body>Unhandled exception: Schema enforcement failed\n</body>\n</html>
```
maia: They say their client immediately throws a JSON parse error because Content-Type is application/json (they set Accept) but body is HTML.
jordan: Aha — gateway is returning our internal HTML diagnostic page for enforcement failures instead of a JSON error. Looks like a regression in the error handler that sets content-type based on the error template. Also possible model produced invalid JSON and our enforcement path triggered, returning the HTML debug page to clients that asked for json.
support-bot: Ticket CS-8921 created for ACME. Priority: high. ETA: triage today.
kyle: Short-term workarounds for the customer:
- Set response_format.strict=false to let the model pass through (not ideal for schema guarantees).
- Or set Accept: text/plain so client will treat the body as text and can attempt to sanitize before parsing.
- Client-side: verify Content-Type header before parsing JSON and fail gracefully if it doesn't match.
maia: Customer tried strict=false and the model returned JSON-ish text with trailing commas and a few unquoted keys — still brittle. They want strict enforcement but not the HTML blob.
jordan: Action plan: change gateway so enforcement/errors always return application/json with a structured error payload when Accept includes application/json or when X-Redwood-Expect: application/json header is present. Add header x-redwood-error: json-enforcement and include request_id.
I'll open the PR to change the error middleware and add a unit test for content-type on enforcement failures. Also will add a metric for enforcement-failures -> cs tickets.
kyle: For immediate debugging, check upstream logs for rq_abc123 — I see a 502 from model runtime around 2026-03-14T15:12:05Z that correlates. Might be model produced malformed tokens triggering our validator to crash.
maia: Sending the workaround and ETA to customer now (:thumbsup:). Will follow up once PR merges.
jordan: Thanks. I'll post the PR link here when ready.
kyle: Great — once gateway change is deployed, customers can keep strict=true and get a proper JSON error response instead of an HTML page. :+1:
